convention: The hull box reaches the hull and turret roof; sights, antennas and roof guns are dressing within 0.3 m (bulky) or 0.15 m across (thin); the pivot sits at the centre of the turret ring (a fixed howitzer mount: its trunnion); the muzzle sits at the real barrel length. Box length covers the body (hull plus any armoured turret overhang), centred on the box origin.

thresholds.note: Slice 07's guesses, kept: every fix row below clears them by a wide margin or is named as borderline. muzzle_reach_m is added by lane F-C (the slice set none for muzzles).

height_m.source: same; overall (launcher and sight tops 2.29-2.36 m on the drawing and photo)

turret_ring_x_m.note: The 1981 drawing's turret is drawn further back than the photo shows; the photo (a real vehicle, square-on) governs. The U.S. Army BMP-1 graphic has its turret further forward still. The ring position stays the least certain number here (+-0.15 m).

upper_glacis_deg_above_horizontal.published: 80 deg from vertical for the BMP-1/2 upper plate (10 deg above horizontal)

lower_glacis_deg_above_horizontal.published: 57 deg from vertical for the BMP-1/2 lower plate (33 deg above horizontal)

lower_plate_foot.real: 0.65-0.77 m up, 0.65-0.75 m behind the nose, where the hull underside takes over above the sprocket
lower_plate_foot.model: runs down to the belly at 0.42 m, 0.77 m behind the nose

glacis.reading: The real nose sits 0.25-0.3 m higher. From it the upper plate rises gently (10-12 deg) and the lower plate drops a short way, then the belly. The model's low nose makes its upper glacis fall 4 deg too steeply and stretches its lower plate down to the belly: exactly the user's note.

overlays.reading: Top of silhouette every 0.25 m from the rear; the forward stations are the gun. The pink band over the model's nose is the higher real nose.

verdicts.why: 2.45 m is the launcher and sight tops. The art's roof (2.21 m) stays inside tolerance.

verdicts.why: The ring centre is 0.09 m ahead of hull centre: 0.2 m off, just over the 0.15 m threshold (borderline).

verdicts.source: muzzle 2.48 m (photo) and 2.50 m (drawing) ahead of hull centre
verdicts.why: The frame puts the muzzle at 3.13 m, 0.24 m behind the nose; the real 30 mm ends 0.88 m behind it. 0.65 m off.

dressing_conflicts.why: 0.01 m past the 0.3 m bulky allowance on a 2.15 m box: settle with the other sight heads (decisions.md FC3), or seat the housings 0.01 m lower.

notes.note: front slopes down too much, bottom should actually slope up more
notes.why: The glacis geometry (bmp.py Bmp2 hull_upper/hull_lower): raise the nose from 0.95 to about 1.2 m, flatten the upper plate to 10-12 deg, end the lower plate at about 0.7 m. The frame is unaffected (see glacis).

The drawing's ring centre is +0.27 m.

The hull is 0.2 m low (roof 1.62 against 1.8-1.9 m), and so is the turret (2.16 against 2.37 m). The nose is 0.35-0.4 m low, with the upper glacis 10 deg too steep and the lower one 20 deg too shallow: the BRM's note, on the hull it shares (S13).
